Machine learning approaches have also been assessed under the PATH framework...

Xu et al. (2024). 

This study compared different methods for generating risk-based subgroups for heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) analysis in a randomized clinical trial (ASPREE). Comparison was done between:

1. A semi-parametric Cox proportional hazards model (extant risk model)

2. A decision tree

3. A random forest

Similarly to our loigistic regression model, each model was used to:

1. Predict baseline outcome risk,

2. Partition participants into risk-based subgroups, (Quintiles for RF)

3. Estimate treatment effects within those subgroups.

Cox model was the only one to show significant HTE on the absolute scale.

It would be interesting to see how this model may perform in risk based subgrouping against the established framework. Random Forest appears to be the best option, could use quintiles and deciles or quartiles like in previous approach.

In line with PATH, quartiles could be plotted in terms of relative risk and absolute treatment effect.
